actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species is known from four localities in the semi-deciduous forest of the Brazilian central plateau in western Minas Gerais (Araguari, Rio Jordão) and southern Goiás states (Anápolis; Percequillo, 1998), and in forested habitats within the Cerrado biome of Federal District and northern Goiás state: Fazenda Fiandeira, Parque Nacional da Chapada dos Veadeiros, 65 km SSW Cavalcante; Fazenda Cadoz, Mimoso de Goiás; Terra Ronca State Park and Brasília National Park (Bonvicino et al. 1998, Bonvicino et al. 2011, Ribeiro 2015).
documentation.population: This rodent is known from only four localities and there is no information about its population or abundance. Of the four localities where it has been recorded, two have been completed destroyed due to agricultural expansion.
documentation.habitats: This species is regarded as a forest-dweller (Weksler 1996, Percequillo 1998), inhabiting gallery forests and a luxuriant semi-deciduous forest. This species is reported from habitats from 700 to 900 m (Eisenberg and Redford 1999). Recent published data suggest that it also occurs in Cerrado habitats, such as cerradão (a dry woodland savanna), cerrado sensu stricto, and campo úmido (both open habitats), although two specimens were captured in the ecotone with gallery forest (Bonvicino et al. 1998).
documentation.threats: The major threats to this species are habitat destruction and fragmentation for conversion to agriculture, livestock and logging (Percequillo and Weksler 2008).
documentation.measures: This rodent occurs in several protected areas (D. Tirira pers. comm).
documentation.rationale: This species is listed as Vulnerable because its area of occupancy (AOO) is less than 2,000 km², the species is known from only four locations and two have been completely destroyed due to agricultural conversion, and the extent of occurrence and habitat quality have continued to decline.
